candidate.claim: collect uses forEach with an async callback and returns results immediately, so promises are never awaited and the returned array is always empty.
candidate.title: async forEach never awaited returns empty results

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback whose awaited push at src/analytics.ts:7 is never awaited by collect, which returns results at src/analytics.ts:12 immediately after the synchronous forEach call.

candidate.claim: buildSummary appends to module-level totals on every call and then summarizes totals, so a second call double-counts prior entries.
candidate.title: module accumulator makes buildSummary double-count

verifier.reason: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post which pushes onto the module-level totals declared at src/ledger.ts:6 and defined at src/ledger.ts:8-9, then iterates all of totals without any reset, so a second call re-includes and re-counts prior entries.

candidate.claim: validate uses OR instead of AND for missing checks, so each condition is always true and errors are always reported even for complete payloads.
candidate.title: OR instead of AND makes validation always fail

verifier.reason: At src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11, the conditions using !== undefined || !== null are tautologies because any value differs from at least one of undefined/null, so both errors are unconditionally pushed even for complete payloads.

candidate.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before calling store.get, so the read can race the write and return the old token.
candidate.title: missing await on save races subsequent get

verifier.reason: The code at src/session.ts:11 calls store.save(userId, token) without await while save returns Promise<void> at src/session.ts:2, then immediately returns store.get(userId) at src/session.ts:12, so the read can race the write.

candidate.claim: start overwrites this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing any existing interval, leaking the prior timer on repeated calls.
candidate.title: timer handle replaced without clearing existing interval

verifier.reason: The start method at src/scheduler.ts:7-11 assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no preceding clearInterval or guard on an existing timer, so repeated calls orphan the prior interval.

candidate.claim: pageSlice computes end as start+size then slices to end+1, returning size+1 items instead of one page.
candidate.title: off-by-one slice returns extra element

verifier.reason: Confirmed: src/paging.ts:9 sets end as start+size and src/paging.ts:10 returns items.slice(start, end + 1), and since slice's end is exclusive this returns size+1 items when available.

candidate.claim: sort without a numeric comparator sorts numbers lexicographically, so sortScores and topScore return wrong order for values like 10 and 9.
candidate.title: numeric sort without comparator orders lexicographically

verifier.reason: The code at src/scores.ts:2 uses scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, which sorts numbers lexicographically as strings, and topScore at src/scores.ts:7 returns the last sorted element, so values like 10 and 9 are ordered incorrectly.

candidate.claim: withinQuota uses strict less-than while the contract says max is inclusive, so using exactly the maximum is incorrectly rejected.
candidate.title: exclusive comparison violates inclusive quota

verifier.reason: The comment at src/quota.ts:2 states max is inclusive for exactly the maximum, but src/quota.ts:6 returns used + amount < max, which is false when used + amount equals max.
